candidates.explanation: The login error is `needLoginViaProvider:google`, so the stored user's `provider` is `google` instead of `email`. `AuthService.register` goes through `UsersService.create`, and it never passes a provider, because the register DTO has no provider field. `create` is therefore the only place that can assign the provider for email sign-ups. The part that builds the user (default provider) is cut off in the snippet, so this is inferred. It most likely defaults to or hard-codes the wrong value instead of `AuthProvidersEnum.email`. The default should be `createUserDto.provider ?? AuthProvidersEnum.email`.

For an inactive user found by email, this branch overwrites `provider` and `socialId` with the social login's values. That lets any Google login using the same email take over an unconfirmed email account and set its provider to google. The branch should not rewrite the provider of an existing email account. This is a less likely cause for this report, since the user never touched Google.

After confirmation it saves the whole user object through `UsersService.update`. If the update path does not preserve the provider, this step could also change it. This is a weaker suspect, because the snippet shows only the status change.

fix.description: In UsersService.create, set `provider: createUserDto.provider ?? AuthProvidersEnum.email` when building the user passed to the repository. Remove any hard-coded or incorrect default such as google. Also remove the inactive-user provider override in validateSocialLogin, so an unconfirmed email account is not taken over by a social provider.

candidates.explanation: The login error is `needLoginViaProvider:google`, so the stored user's `provider` is `google` instead of `email`. `AuthService.register` goes through `UsersService.create`, and it never passes a provider, because the register DTO has no provider field. `create` is therefore the only place that can assign the provider for email sign-ups. The part that builds the user (default provider) is cut off in the snippet, so this is inferred. It most likely defaults to or hard-codes the wrong value instead of `AuthProvidersEnum.email`. The default should be `createUserDto.provider ?? AuthProvidersEnum.email`.

For an inactive user found by email, this branch overwrites `provider` and `socialId` with the social login's values. That lets any Google login using the same email take over an unconfirmed email account and set its provider to google. The branch should not rewrite the provider of an existing email account. This is a less likely cause for this report, since the user never touched Google.

After confirmation it saves the whole user object through `UsersService.update`. If the update path does not preserve the provider, this step could also change it. This is a weaker suspect, because the snippet shows only the status change.

fix.description: In UsersService.create, set `provider: createUserDto.provider ?? AuthProvidersEnum.email` when building the user passed to the repository. Remove any hard-coded or incorrect default such as google. Also remove the inactive-user provider override in validateSocialLogin, so an unconfirmed email account is not taken over by a social provider.
